note: A one-pixel green pinstripe runs the whole length of the pool's east edge, and nothing else: seen from straight above at `0,14,4.6,3.1416,1.5708` with a 0.5 eye, pixels down x=1143 of a 1280-wide picture come out near (97,162,25) — grass green — while the west, north and south edges come out teal. The camera is 14 m up over the pool's centre, so the ray to that edge is tilted 20 degrees off vertical and sees a sliver of the east wall's INNER face (a pick there names poolEast at y -0.03, just above the water) and the 2 cm top ledge of the wet band, where the other three walls show nothing of themselves. Which of those is painting the line is what this asks: each case switches one suspect out and `tools/scanline.js` reads the same row of the same camera in every picture it saves.
